title: Implement secure communication channels: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: For a voice, video, remote-admin, provider, or transport channel, what identity, endpoint, scope, media/data governance, evidence, and revocation decision makes it securely usable?
focalInsight: A channel is secure only across its full lifecycle: authorized setup, protected/observed use, and revocation/evidence at completion.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Secure Channel
nodes.definition: Communication path with defined endpoints, identity, protection, authorization, monitoring, failure behavior, and lifecycle governance.
nodes.detail: Communication path with defined endpoints, identity, protection, authorization, monitoring, failure behavior, and lifecycle governance.
nodes.decision: Select channel controls from data/media, threat, endpoint trust, duration, and operational need.
nodes.failureExample: An encrypted channel to an unmanaged endpoint exposes data after decryption.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A secure channel includes endpoint trust and lifecycle, not just encryption.

nodes.label: Remote Access
nodes.definition: Privileged or user remote connection to internal resources through an approved, authenticated, scoped path.
nodes.detail: Privileged or user remote connection to internal resources through an approved, authenticated, scoped path.
nodes.decision: Require MFA, managed endpoint/jump/broker, least privilege, session evidence, time bounds, and revocation.
nodes.failureExample: A vendor keeps permanent remote administrator access after maintenance ends.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Remote admin access needs scope, time limit, evidence, and revocation.

nodes.label: Voice Video Security
nodes.definition: Protection of live media, chat/files, recordings, transcripts, rooms/devices, and collaboration identity/authorization.
nodes.detail: Protection of live media, chat/files, recordings, transcripts, rooms/devices, and collaboration identity/authorization.
nodes.decision: Govern participant admission, encryption endpoints, recording/screen-share authority, retention, client updates, and moderation.
nodes.failureExample: A meeting is encrypted but an unauthorized participant records sensitive screens.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Voice/video security includes participant and recording governance.

nodes.label: Third Party Connectivity
nodes.definition: Network or support access involving an external carrier, supplier, hardware vendor, or partner.
nodes.detail: Network or support access involving an external carrier, supplier, hardware vendor, or partner.
nodes.decision: Define boundary, identity, least privilege, route/data protection, logs, notification, support window, contract, and exit.
nodes.failureExample: A provider support tunnel remains active with shared credentials and no logs.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Third-party connectivity needs contractual and technical lifecycle controls.

nodes.label: VPN
nodes.definition: Tunnel that protects selected traffic between defined endpoints across an untrusted/intermediate network.
nodes.detail: Tunnel that protects selected traffic between defined endpoints across an untrusted/intermediate network.
nodes.decision: Choose endpoint identity, selectors/split routing, device posture, logging, key lifecycle, and termination/authorization boundary.
nodes.failureExample: A VPN user can route to every subnet because selectors and authorization are broad.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: VPN protects a path; policy defines reachable resources.

nodes.label: TLS
nodes.definition: Application-session protection between authenticated TLS endpoints.
nodes.detail: Application-session protection between authenticated TLS endpoints.
nodes.decision: Validate certificate/hostname, locate termination, manage versions/keys, and protect upstream/downstream paths.
nodes.failureExample: TLS ends at a proxy and traffic to an internal service is unprotected.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: TLS claim requires named endpoints and onward-path review.

nodes.label: Ssh
nodes.definition: Secure remote administrative/session transport with host and user authentication.
nodes.detail: Secure remote administrative/session transport with host and user authentication.
nodes.decision: Use approved jump paths, host-key verification, least privilege, logging, session control, and credential/key lifecycle.
nodes.failureExample: An administrator accepts a changed host key and sends commands to an impostor.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: SSH requires host identity verification as well as user login.

nodes.label: Backhaul
nodes.definition: Transport connecting access/edge sites to core/provider services, often with carrier, capacity, route, and latency dependencies.
nodes.detail: Transport connecting access/edge sites to core/provider services, often with carrier, capacity, route, and latency dependencies.
nodes.decision: Assess encryption endpoint, provider boundary, resiliency, monitoring, jurisdiction, and fallback.
nodes.failureExample: A single carrier backhaul outage isolates remote sites despite local redundancy.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Backhaul is a service path with provider and availability dependencies.
